title: Priority queue deadlock during KV cache invalidation under promotional surge
creator: Amina Patel
description: Summary: On 2026-02-10 during a marketing-driven promotional traffic spike, requests routed to primary region (us-west-2) caused a cascade: stale KV cache invalidation events collided with a global priority-queue lock, producing head-of-line blocking. Latency SLOs were missed for 99th percentile generation latency across both primary and failing-over secondary region (eu-west-1) as regional failover attempted to shift traffic. The incident lasted ~45 minutes with a targeted SLO (p99 <= 200ms) breaching to ~950ms and a peak error spike of 6% 5xxs from overloaded inference workers.
timeline: 2026-02-10T09:41:00Z - Promotional campaign launches; traffic spike observed +420% baseline to API gateway
2026-02-10T09:43:30Z - us-west-2 KV cache invalidation job begins to run to reconcile stale prefixes after model rollout
2026-02-10T09:44:15Z - Priority queue global lock acquired by cache invalidation worker shard; high-priority inference requests begin queueing
2026-02-10T09:45:00Z - Autoscaling reacts but slow warm-up causes worker saturation; p95/p99 latency climbs rapidly
2026-02-10T09:47:20Z - Circuit breakers for fallback to eu-west-1 start flipping due to elevated latency; simultaneous failover increases cross-region fanout
2026-02-10T09:50:00Z - Engineering on-call pages; initial mitigation: abort KV invalidation job and release locks
2026-02-10T09:53:10Z - Partial recovery as queue drains; p99 drops but remains above SLO due to backlog and cold workers
2026-02-10T10:26:00Z - Full recovery after manual traffic shaping and targeted reroutes to warm instances; incident declared over at 10:30
impact_metrics: p99 latency target 200ms -> observed ~950ms for duration. Error rate 0.4% -> peaked 6% 5xx. Total affected requests approx 320k during 45 minutes. Customer visible failures: some streaming responses truncated, 2 high-volume customers reported degraded latency for 15-30 minutes.
root_cause: Three-way interaction: (1) a scheduled KV cache reconciliation job acquired a global priority-queue lock for shard compaction; (2) promotional spike massively increased high-priority request arrivals producing head-of-line blocking; (3) circuit-breaker hysteresis and cross-region failover policy amplified load on secondary region, creating backpressure and slow warm-up of new workers. The cache invalidation job lacked per-shard contention controls and did not respect dynamic load signals.
contributing_factors: KV invalidation implemented with coarse-grained global lock for simplicity (single lock by shard group)
No admission control for the invalidation job under high API load
Circuit breaker hysteresis thresholds were conservative and allowed simultaneous failover into already congested region
Autoscaling warm-up time for inference workers is non-trivial (GPU provisioning + model load), not accounted for in failover logic
Monitoring lacked an early composite signal combining priority-queue depth + KV-lock hold time to trigger preemptive shedding
short_term_mitigations: Immediately aborted the KV reconciliation job and released locks (done during incident)
Applied temporary traffic shaping at the edge to limit promotional burst per-customer while nodes warmed (done)
Lowered circuit-breaker sensitivity for eu-west-1 to reduce simultaneous failover (done)
Manually pre-warmed a pool of inference workers in eu-west-1 for 30 minutes to accelerate recovery (done)
long_term_mitigations: Replace global priority-queue lock with fine-grained per-shard lock and lock timeout semantics (owner: Carlos Nguyen, due: 2026-03-12)
Rework KV invalidation to event-driven per-prefix invalidation that respects current load signals (owner: Mei Tan, due: 2026-04-02)
Implement admission control so background maintenance jobs will back off when priority-queue depth > threshold (owner: Priya Shah, due: 2026-03-20)
Add composite SLO guard in monitoring that correlates priority-queue depth, lock hold time, and cross-region failover rate to trigger automated soft-shed policies (owner: SRE Team, due: 2026-03-05)
Tune circuit-breaker hysteresis to include warmup-aware thresholds and staggered failover to avoid synchronized cross-region spikes (owner: Reliability PM - Jordan Lewis, due: 2026-03-18)
Improve autoscaling warm-start by maintaining a small always-warm standby pool for each region serving bursty workload classes (owner: Infra - Elena Morales, due: 2026-04-09)
Create a promotional traffic runbook with recommended pre-warm steps and API rate guidance for customers (owner: Solutions Eng - Luis Romero, due: 2026-03-01)
Add canary ramp feature in the routing layer to incrementally shift percent traffic during rollouts/promos (owner: Routing Team, due: 2026-05-01)
Add an automated safeguard to prevent background maintenance jobs from acquiring priority locks when estimated Q depth > X (owner: Cache Team, due: 2026-03-12)

monitoring_changes: Create composite alert: high_priority_blocking (priority_queue_depth > 500 AND kv.lock_hold_time_seconds > 5s)
Add dashboard: promotional-burst SLO-tracker (p50/p95/p99, error-rate, circuit-breaker flips, warm-pool utilization)
postmortem_notes: Design feedback: move maintenance UI to show live lock contention per shard so operators can make informed aborts
PM decision: promotional campaigns must be coordinated with SRE at least 48 hours in advance for high-risk customers
Trade-off: warm standby pools increase cost; estimate a 3.2% uplift in monthly infra spend for p99-sensitive tiers
Follow-up: schedule a runbook tabletop exercise for promotional surge in next on-call rotation
closure_criteria: Per-shard lock implementation merged and deployed to canary
Event-driven KV invalidation prototype validated under synthetic promo traffic
Composite alert firing correctly and paging is tested
Circuit-breaker warmup-aware policy implemented and chaos-tested (no synchronized failover in simulation)
Promotional runbook published and at least one customer campaign coordinated using runbook
